content:
We have now come to the end of the dedication offerings of Numbers 7.
Over many studies we have walked through every vessel, every animal, every number; the silver plate, the silver bowl, the golden spoon, the young bull, the ram, the one-year-old lamb, the sin offering goat, and the peace offerings in all their abundance. Today we stand back and look at the complete summary. Numbers 7:84-88 gives us the total of everything that was offered across all twelve tribes over twelve days. And when we add it all up, the grand total of animals sacrificed was 252. That number is not the end of the story. It is, in fact, one more sermon written in numbers.

Here is the full summary of all the animals offered. There were 36 young bulls in total; 12 from the burnt offering and 24 from the peace offering. There were 72 rams in total; 12 from the burnt offering and 60 from the peace offering. There were 72 male lambs of the first year; 12 from the burnt offering and 60 from the peace offering. There were 72 male goats; 12 from the sin offering and 60 from the peace offering. Add these together: 36 + 72 + 72 + 72 = 252 animals. Twelve tribes. Twelve days.
One offering repeated twelve times. And the grand total of everything laid on the altar of dedication was 252.

Before we look at the number 252 itself, there is a pattern hidden in the structure of these offerings that must not be missed. Twelve tribes offered for twelve days. Twelve multiplied by twelve gives us 144. This number appears in a remarkable place in the New Testament. Revelation 7:4 says: “And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000, sealed from every tribe of the sons of Israel.” And Revelation 14:1 shows the 144,000 standing on Mount Zion with the Lamb, having the Father’s name written on their foreheads. The 144,000 is the Bride of Christ; the sealed, complete, covenant assembly of the redeemed who stand before Yahweh in the fullness of His purposes.

Now notice how the number arrives. 12 multiplied by 12 gives 144.
And 144 multiplied by 1,000 gives 144,000. The 1,000 in Scripture speaks of fullness and completeness; “a thousand years in Your sight are like a watch in the night” (Psalm 90:4). It also connects to the thousand-year reign of Christ described in Revelation 20, the full and complete period of His kingdom rule before the eternal age begins. So the 144,000 is the outcome of the complete covenant structure of twelve tribes (12 × 12 = 144) brought to its full and complete expression (144 × 1,000).

The twelve leaders offering for twelve days in Numbers 7 were already encoding the pattern of the complete covenant assembly that would one day stand before the throne. The sacrifices of the wilderness dedication were already pointing to the birth of the Bride of Christ.

Now we look at the number 252 itself. When we read the digits individually; 2, 5, 2 a beautiful and precise spiritual pattern emerges. The first number is 2. The middle number is 5. And the last number is 2 again. Two, five, two. Each of these has a clear and consistent meaning in Scripture.

The number 2 is the number of witness and testimony. Deuteronomy 19:15 says: “A matter shall be established by the testimony of two witnesses.” Matthew 18:16 confirms the same principle in the mouth of Christ. Two is the number by which truth is established and confirmed. Two tablets of the covenant. Two cherubim over the mercy seat. Two angels at the resurrection. Two is the number of confirmed, established, unshakeable testimony. And 2 also speaks of union; two becoming one. Genesis 2:24: “The two shall become one flesh.” The two witnesses also speak of the two great divisions of Scripture; the Old Testament and the New Testament both bearing witness to the same Christ. Jesus Himself said I came to fulfil the Law and the Prophets.

The number 5 is the number of grace. The five books of Moses. The five loaves that fed five thousand. Five is consistently the number of what God provides by His undeserved favour. And in Leviticus 1-5, there are precisely five major offerings: the burnt offering, the grain offering, the peace offering, the sin offering, and the trespass offering. Five offerings. Five books of Torah. Christ completed every single one. He was the burnt offering of total surrender. He was the grain offering of a perfect sinless life. He was the peace offering that restored fellowship between man and God. He was the sin offering who bore the guilt and carried it away. He was the trespass offering who paid every individual debt of every individual offence. The five of the Torah is fulfilled completely in Christ.

Now read 252 as a sentence: two, five, two; witness, grace, witness. The testimony of the Old Testament, the grace of Christ’s complete five-fold sacrifice, confirmed by the testimony of the New Testament. The 252 animals on the altar of dedication were declaring from the wilderness what the whole of Scripture would one day say plainly: grace; the complete, five-fold, Torah-fulfilling sacrifice of Christ; witnessed on both sides by the unbreakable double testimony of the Word of God. Old Testament witness. Five-fold grace of Christ. New Testament witness.
2 - 5 - 2.

The 252 animals of the dedication offering are a complete summary of what Christ accomplished. Every offering type present; burnt, grain, peace, sin, and trespass was fulfilled in Him. Every tribe present; all twelve, none missing was represented before the altar. Every day covered all twelve, without a single gap speaks of a redemption that covers every day of every life of every person who comes through it. The 252 is not a random total. It is a number that carries the full weight of the five-fold sacrifice, established by two-sided testimony, pointing forward to the 144,000 who will stand before the throne as the complete covenant assembly of the redeemed.

And so the chapter that began with the dedication of the altar ends with the voice. After all 252 animals, after all twelve leaders, after all twelve days; Numbers 7:89 records that Moses went into the tabernacle and heard the voice of Yahweh speaking to him from between the cherubim above the mercy seat. The offering came first. The voice came after. The 252 were placed on the altar, and then God spoke. This is the pattern of the whole chapter and the pattern of the whole gospel:
the sacrifice is complete, the testimony is established, the grace has been fully displayed, the covenant assembly is being formed; and into the silence after the last offering, the voice of Yahweh speaks. He always speaks after the offering has been laid down.

title: Prayer
text:
Oh Holy Father, Every number in Your Word is a sermon. Every total on Your altar is a declaration. We thank You for the 252; for the witness of the Old Testament, the five-fold grace of Christ completing every offering of the Torah, and the witness of the New Testament confirming what was always true.
We thank You that the 12 times 12 of the twelve tribes over twelve days is already encoding the 144,000 who will stand before the throne; that the wilderness dedication offerings were already pointing to the Bride of Christ who will one day stand on Mount Zion with the Lamb. We thank You for the voice that came after the last offering in Numbers 7:89. Help us today to lay the offering down first; to bring the whole of what we are before the altar and then to wait in the silence for the voice that always comes after the offering has been placed. In Christ’s name, amen.
